# 27 — AI Action Registry

**Status:** PROPOSAL. Machine-readable version: [data/ai-tools-proposal.json](data/ai-tools-proposal.json), generated by `tools/ai_tools.py`. Every tool maps to an existing route, library function or RPC (checked 2026-11-20), or to a domain module approved in doc 21 (marked `to_create`).

## Totals

35 tools: **14 read · 7 draft · 9 write · 5 high-impact**, plus 5 capabilities deliberately **excluded** from AI.

## Tool contract (every tool)

```ts
type AiTool<I, O> = {
  name: string;                       // snake_case, stable
  risk: 'read' | 'draft' | 'write' | 'high';
  description: string;                // what the model sees; plain language
  input: z.ZodType<I>;                // strict; event_id/org_id injected from context, never from the model
  output: z.ZodType<O>;               // what goes back to the model (redacted, doc 32)
  canUse: (caller) => Promise<boolean>;   // the SAME helper the page/route uses (portalAuth, resolve*Capability, …)
  execute: (caller, input) => Promise<O>; // read/draft: runs; write/high: builds a proposal
  apply?: (caller, proposal) => Promise<Result>; // write/high: after approval, via domain module
};
```

- **Offered tools are filtered by `canUse` before the model sees them**, so the model never learns about actions the user can't take. The server still re-checks on every call.
- **`event_id` and `organization_id` come from the context engine** (doc 26), never from model arguments. This blocks cross-event or cross-organisation leakage through tool arguments.
- **Inputs are validated with zod (strict).** One repair round is allowed; then the call stops (doc 25).

## By risk

| Risk | Tools | Approval |
|---|---|---|
| **Read** | `search_navigation`, `navigate_to`, `get_event_summary`, `get_event_readiness`, `list_speakers`, `get_agenda`, `check_schedule_conflicts`, `list_attendees`, `list_participants`, `list_tasks`, `list_vendor_items`, `list_checklist`, `get_run_of_show`, `get_recent_activity` | None. Runs as the user. |
| **Draft** | `draft_text`, `draft_networking_questions`, `draft_notification`, `draft_agenda`, `draft_run_of_show`, `parse_document`, `propose_field_mapping` | No data change. The output is an editable draft or staging. |
| **Write** | `upsert_speaker`, `upsert_sessions`, `upsert_faqs`, `update_event_details`, `apply_import`, `create_planner_tasks`, `upsert_participants`, `upsert_flights_hotels`, `upsert_run_of_show` | A **proposal** with before/after diff, approved per proposal |
| **High impact** | `bulk_update`, `delete_records`, `add_event_members` (sends access-code emails), `schedule_push_notification`, `set_event_visibility` | **Typed confirmation** showing the exact count and consequences. Never in the background. |
| **Excluded** | Planner permission changes; platform admin (organisations, products, moderation); account creation and make-admin; raw SQL, HTTP, files or shell; passport and dietary data in context | Not available to AI |

## Proposal lifecycle (Portal 2.0 §16)

`drafted → shown (diff) → approved | rejected | edited → revalidated (permissions + record versions unchanged) → executed → audited`

- A proposal is bound to **user, organisation, event and each record's `updated_at`**. If anything changed, it becomes **stale**, and a fresh proposal is needed.
- An approved proposal can't be modified. Editing creates a new proposal.
- Execution goes through the domain module, so the existing trigger audit (`event_content_audit_log`) records the actor as the **user**, and `ai_action_log` adds the AI context.

## Reactive navigation (§15.4)

`search_navigation` and `navigate_to` only return routes from `data/routes.json`, filtered by products and permissions:
- "Where do I configure networking?" opens People › Networking.
- "Open flights" opens Logistics › Travel, filtered to flights.

Unknown features get "Studio doesn't have that". The model never invents a URL.
